headline: High: Perplexity can ingest uploaded files and browse externally, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error risk when paired with a non-executing but content-producing repo/list agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a static awesome-list repo with no runtime ingestion path, while B can browse and analyze uploaded documents. There is no documented shared channel or automatic handoff between them, so prompt injection is not a default pathway. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or file upload into B, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A's text into B as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to ingest A-derived files without review, malicious content in those files can steer B.
mitigations: Keep A and B separated by a human review step before any copy/paste.
Strip instructions from any A-derived text before uploading to B.
Use a fixed prompt template in B that ignores embedded directives.
Mark A outputs as untrusted content in the workflow.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B processes search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context, and sends calls to vendor/search APIs. If A-derived files or notes are uploaded into B, content can leave the local environment through B's vendor-hosted backend. The pairwise leakage path exists in default B usage, though A itself is not a data source by default.
conditions: IF A-derived documents are uploaded into B, their contents may be transmitted to vendor/search services.
IF the workflow uses B's browsing context for sensitive material, that material can persist in vendor-hosted context.
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive A-derived artifacts into B.
Use redacted copies before analysis in B.
Restrict B to non-sensitive queries only.
Clear B sessions after each task.
Prefer local-only tools for any confidential material.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or execution surface, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B cannot write files or modify git state and only has vendor-only egress plus browser access. Because neither agent can write the same local directory or shared mutable resource, capability conflict is limited to read-only overlap and is not a meaningful default hazard.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk increases.
IF B is wrapped with additional filesystem or git permissions not shown here, contention can emerge.
mitigations: Keep B's current no-write permissions unchanged.
Avoid placing A and B behind a shared writable workspace.
Use read-only mounts for any shared inputs.
Add orchestration-level locking if future write access is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated list, so its outputs can be treated as authoritative references, and B is an answer engine that renders cited results from browsing. If A-derived recommendations are fed into B without verification, B can amplify stale or incorrect entries into user-facing answers. The pathway is plausible in default workflows even though A is not an active agent.
conditions: IF A's curated entries are copied into B as factual ground truth, B may propagate errors.
IF B is asked to summarize A without independent verification, stale list items can be presented as current.
mitigations: Require B to verify A-derived claims against primary sources.
Label A as a secondary source in prompts.
Add a citation-check step before publishing B's output.
Use freshness timestamps when available.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source repository with no touched data classes, while B is a vendor-hosted search/RAG service that handles search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented here, so compliance risk is limited to general policy mismatch if sensitive data is introduced into B. The other agent is not cited for a residency violation because none is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into B, vendor-hosted processing may violate local policy.
IF an organization requires local-only retention for search artifacts, B's hosted context can conflict.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into B.
Review B's privacy policy before use.
Use anonymized queries and documents.
Keep A as a public reference only.
